text:
alex: heads up — after landing my batch-merge improvement (PR #4821) we're seeing KV cache slot thrash on long-context workloads. memory climbs and tail latency spikes. repro on nightly stress harness.

maya: can you paste the profiler flame or summary? is this before or after the slot-stitch change? :thinking: 

alex: after. short summary from perf run:
```
KV-store: high allocs in slot_stitch(); 40% CPU spent in merge_walk_and_claim();
continuous-batcher: more small merged batches -> increased fragment churn
eviction: async reclaim queue depth spikes, latency to reclaim grows
```

chris: hmm. small merged batches sounds like the batching heuristic split too aggressively. Are we creating more head-of-line (HOL) blocking because some merges can't claim contiguous KV ranges?

alex: exactly. when a merged batch contains queries that map to adjacent but owned-by-different-threads slots, slot_stitch tries to stitch but fails often and leaves many tiny fragments. Those fragments get evicted then re-populated by subsequent tokens. Net effect: memory oscillates and we thrash evict/repopulate.

leo: do you have a minimal repro? i can run the mem profiler with per-slot histograms.

alex: yep repro is in: ci/perf/longctx_kv_thrash.yaml (1000 requests, 4 concurrent sessions, seq_len=32->2048 ramp). ran with `--kv-debug=slot-trace` and captured logs. excerpt: 
```
[00:02:13] slot_stitch: claim failed: owner=42 expected=41 slot=0x7f4a3c
[00:02:13] create_fragment: size=128 owner=43 frag_id=0x9a1
[00:02:14] evict_async: queued frag_id=0x9a1 age=1ms
[00:02:14] refill: load shard 5 frag_id=0x9a1 cache_miss
```

maya: that log shows rapid create->evict->refill loop. Could be allocator fragmentation too. Do we have per-shard alloc stats?

alex: attached in the CI artifact but TL;DR: free_list lengths bounce and slab reclaim is frequent. The stitch path holds the per-shard mutex longer under contention, so other threads time out and create competing fragments.

tasha: suggestion: make the stitch optimistic and fall back to a deferred stitch queue instead of spinning for the claim. That would reduce immediate fragment churn and allow coalescing later. Would that still honor latency SLOs?

chris: also consider batching heuristic change: prefer merge only when >N contiguous owners agree, otherwise leave as separate batches. Fewer incorrect stitches -> fewer tiny fragments. We had a similar rule in 2022 for GPU-prefetching.

leo: i'll try two experiments: 1) optimistic-defer-stitch (no claim spin, enqueue for background coalesce), 2) increase contiguous-owner threshold from 1 -> 3. will run on the nightly harness.

perf-bot: perf run queued: job/1987-kv-thrash-opt1 on perf-ci (expected ~30m).

alex: thanks. one more datapoint — with the current change the long-tail allocations are almost all for 'kv_fragment' objects, not general GC. so tuning allocator won't fully fix it. need fewer frag creates.

maya: what about read-path: can we make reads tolerant of missing contiguous KV? i.e., if prefix cache hit fails to find a stitched span, fall back to on-demand merge without creating a persistent fragment (transient reader cache).

chris: that's a good idea for the hot-path. transient fragments that are not inserted into global cache avoid eviction churn. but need to ensure we don't regress tail latency for requests that would have benefited from an existing fragment. maybe hybrid: create persistent fragment only when access count > K within window.

tasha: we should also add a perf regression test that triggers HOL blocking: multi-tenant mixed-latency workload with controlled owner interleaving. currently our tests focus on throughput.

alex: agreed — will add a CI scenario and instrument per-slot wait times (histogram buckets). also will add a debug flag to toggle optimistic stitch.

leo: early results from opt-defer (first 12m): memory growth curve flattened, max RSS down ~18%, p99 latency down ~220ms on long ctx. contiguous-owner-threshold change alone reduced frag creation by ~30% but left some HOL stalls.

maya: that's promising. any new regressions on short-context workloads?

leo: none observed in quick smoke. need longer runs for SLO confidence.

chris: plan then: merge optimistic-defer as guarded feature flag + threshold bump, add CI regression test, and instrument slot claim latencies. roll out to canary. if stable, flip default.

alex: I'll file a follow-up PR to add the CI test and the opt-stitch flag. PR link will be posted here when ready. thanks all. :heart: 

perf-bot: job/1987-kv-thrash-opt1 completed: peak-rss=0.82x baseline, p99=0.87x baseline, frag-creations=0.65x baseline. logs: https://ci.internal/perf/1987/artifacts

maya: nice. canary when green.

chris: small note — add a debug metric `kv.stitch.deferred_queue_len` so we can monitor queue growth in prod if we enable optimistic-defer.

alex: will add metric. closing for now, will update thread with PRs and canary results.
